scope: Proposition 4.1 (Uniform bulk conditional averaging) of the manuscript “Conformal universality of bulk Ising correlations under weak interactions” (preprints/Conformal-universality-of-bulk-Ising-correlations-under-weak-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8a815e7845436e07), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are constants C < ∞ and ℓ0 < ∞ with the following property. Fix ℓ = R/s ≥ ℓ0. For all sufficiently large s, with its threshold allowed to depend on ℓ, let F be any bounded lattice function supported in Bs(0). Put m(F) = ECF, dR(F) = E+ disk(4R)F − m(F). Then |dR(F)| ≤ C(s/R)d ∥F∥∞, (4.1) ∥PRF − m(F)∥∞ ≤ C|dR(F)| + C(s/R)p ∥F∥∞, (4.2) with (d, p) = ⎧ ⎪ ⎪ ⎨ ⎪ ⎪ ⎩ (1, 3), F even and invariant under right-angle rotations, (1, 2), F even, (1/8, 9/8), F odd. The constants are independent of every sufficiently large fixed ratio. The same conclusion holds along ratios tending to a fixed ℓ ≥ ℓ0, after harmless changes in the thresholds.
